messages:
ashwin: quick proposal — push authz attrs into the edge proxy so routing/quotas can use them. goal: per-org quota accounting + priority routing without hitting auth service on hot path

linda: +1 on reducing auth svc hop, but what attrs exactly? we need to avoid leaking PII into telemetry :lock:

ashwin: thinking minimal set: org_id (hashed), project_id, service_account_id, role (consumer/admin). nothing user-level. header names: `X-RW-Org`, `X-RW-Project`, `X-RW-Service`, `X-RW-Role`

kevin: hashing org_id is fine. what about replay/forgery? headers from clients are untrusted. proxy should verify tokens and stamp headers server-side after validation, not accept client-sent headers.

mikey: implementation note: authn middleware will validate JWT, then set `x-rw-*` headers before envoy LB. we can add an Envoy header_to_metadata filter to drive routing decisions.

sam: for console dashboards we need the telemetry pipeline to include org/project tags. current metrics are only by model and route. adding org dims will explode cardinality — we should sample and aggregate.

linda: agree on sampling. propose 1% full-org traces for new metric dims, roll up 1h aggregates for cost dashboards, keep raw events for 7d then aggregate to 30d.

kevin: also need to ensure quota enforcement uses strong attribution: request authenticated principal -> authoritative key mapping. If we rely on stamped headers, record signing key id too (`kid`) so audits can trace back.

ashwin: good call. add `X-RW-KID` header (server-stamped). example of the validated flow:

```
client -> edge (validate JWT) -> stamp X-RW-* headers -> route to pool (quota check by org hashed id)
```

mikey: sample Envoy config snippet for routing match (sketch):

```yaml
- match: 
    headers:
      - name: x-rw-org
        present_match: true
  route:
    cluster: org-priority-pool
```

linda: telemetry/PII checklist: hash with salt stored in secrets mgr, never log raw org names, redact in traces. add a regression alert if any raw-org appears in logs. :rotating_light:

sam: UX question — how will this surface in Console? We need a toggle in Routes config: "Enable org-aware routing" with rollout % and a simulation mode that logs decisions without enforcing quotas.

ashwin: agree. rollout plan: 0) implement header stamping + routing rule behind feature flag, 1) simulate for 10% traffic and emit `rw.org.routing.simulation` metric, 2) canary 1% enforce for internal orgs, 3) 25% for paying customers, 4) full. ops-bot: scheduling canary windows?

ops-bot: canary windows OK. suggest nightly low-traffic window + immediate rollback hooks if error rate > 0.5% or 5xx spike. we can auto-disable flag via runbook.

kevin: what about quota accounting semantics during rollout? double-count risk if both old and new paths charge. need a transitional mode: new system reports-only, no debit until cutover. Console should surface "pending quota delta" for each org.

sam: UI will show "Simulated cost impact" with estimate (tokens/sec * projected price). we can reuse current billing estimator.

mikey: telemetry wire format: add `org_hash`, `project_hash`, `service_hash`, `envoy_route` to structured logs. keep fields snake_case for pipeline compatibility. sample event:

```json
{"ts": 1620000000, "org_hash": "a1b2...", "route": "text.generate.v2", "tokens": 24}
```

linda: small perf note — adding header inspection in filter chain adds ~0.2ms p99 currently; acceptable but measure at scale. we should include microbench in perf tests.

ashwin: action items:
- mikey: prototype authn middleware + header stamping (week 1)
- linda: telemetry sampling/retention design + PII audit (week 1)
- kevin: quota transition plan + audit fields (week 1)
- sam: Console UX mock for feature flag + simulation mode (week 2)
- ops-bot: create canary runbook and automated rollback playbook (week 2)

dev-bot: deploy-bot scheduled: canary-feature-flag-ops created (id: canary-7921) :white_check_mark:

ashwin: OK let's sync Thu 10am for API surface review. if no objections by EOD I'll open RFC. :thumbsup:

kevin: no objections from me.

linda: fine from security side, just follow PII checklist.

sam: UX will bring mocks to Thu.

mikey: I'll have prototype slate for review.

ashwin: thanks all! :rocket:
